Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 21. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Јулије и Јулијан“ — Преподобни is the rank and comes off, and the first of the two bare forenames is left. «of Aegina» in the display name is the corpus’s own off saint.gr and this heading does not have it; „презвитер“ is in the body and not in the heading, so it was never a candidate for the form. **The fold is deliberate and forced**: `foldchk.py` returns `julius-the-veteran`, `sr`, for «Јулије», so this is the second folder on the string and **the first time the gate will print a row for it at all**, one holder being below its threshold. The heading offers nothing to break it with — one rank word over two bare forenames. A `READ_FOLDS` key is added for it in the same commit.

birth.note: saint.gr: «ο Άγιος Ιούλιος γεννήθηκε το 330 μ.Χ. στην Αίγινα από εύπορους και ευσεβείς γονείς»; the page's heading dates him «(330 - 407)».

death.note: The page contradicts itself: its heading dates him «(330 - 407)», while its text says «κοιμήθηκε με ειρήνη το έτος 401 μ.Χ., σε ηλικία 71 ετών» — which also does not fit a birth in 330. Both readings are the page's, and the interval holds them both.

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, the elder of its two brothers. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The heading is quoted **whole** on both folders, as §4 requires: a row’s quoted line is the Prologue’s own heading and not the half of it that names this man. **THE DAY IS NOT THE SAME MENOLOGION NUMBER, AND HERE THE TWO BROTHERS DO NOT EVEN SHARE ONE.** This folder’s only other venerated row is Greek and on **31 January**; his brother’s is Greek and on **7 January**; this book keeps them **together** on 21 June. Three numbers for two men who were never apart in either account. That is not a §4 second-day note, which is owed only where a folder already carries a venerated row for this same church on another day, and the `serbian` row was `undocumented` on both. The row goes on the day of the page read, and that this book is the first of the three to keep them on one day is a reading recorded here and in no field. **A `related` ROW THE CORPUS DID NOT HAVE, WRITTEN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Neither folder related the other, although saint.gr’s own two accounts have them resolve together, be ordained together and go out together — the corpus held the companionship in two prose accounts and in no field. This book states the kinship outright, „Рођена браћа“, brothers by birth, which neither other account says. So `related_add` on both, `julius-of-aegina` and `julian-the-deacon-of-aegina`, reciprocal in one batch. **This is not an identification off a name in another man’s life**: the two folders existed, the Greek source already paired them as lifelong companions in both of their own lives, and what this book adds is the degree of the tie and not the fact of it. **A RANK WORD OFF THE HEADING, WRITTEN ONTO A FOLDER THAT LACKED IT.** Преподобни is the heading’s one rank word and §5 maps it to `venerable`. This folder’s `types` were `presbyter` and `preacher` and held no `venerable` at all, saint.gr’s line being «Άγιος Ιούλιος ο Πρεσβύτερος εξ Αιγίνης» and ranking him by his order only. `types_add: ["venerable"]`, on the rule that a rank word in the heading is written. „презвитер“ in the **body** is refused as a confirmation, `presbyter` being on the folder already off another book’s heading and left exactly as it was. `dates` UNTOUCHED. **ONE THING THE TWO BOOKS CANNOT BOTH BE RIGHT ABOUT, AND IT TOUCHES NO FIELD.** This entry has the brothers obtain a charter from the emperor „цара Теодосија Млађег“, Theodosius the Younger, allowing them to pull down idols and build Christian churches throughout the empire. saint.gr’s dates, which are on both folders already, have the deacon die in 391 and the presbyter in 401 or 407 — **all of them before Theodosius the Younger came to the throne at all**. The two readings are irreconcilable as they stand. **Nothing is done to `dates` on either folder**: this book prints no year of any kind, an emperor is no source for a year, a reign is not a date, and a field is not widened or narrowed to accommodate a reign it does not name. The charter is written into both lives as what the book says and the tension is stated as a tension. **It is the author’s to weigh**, since the only ways out of it are to read the epithet as someone else’s or to doubt saint.gr’s years, and neither is a reader’s to do. **AND THE EMPEROR IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN IN THE PROSE, BECAUSE `npm test` CAUGHT IT.** Both paragraphs first read «… from the emperor it calls Theodosius the Younger a charter …» and `related-floor.test.mjs` failed on both, because **`theodosius-the-younger` is a folder and that string is its `display_name` exactly** — §6’s trap for the second time in three days, and the first time this wave has met it on an **emperor**, who is the very kind of name the standing rule says takes no row. The fix was §6’s and not the exclusions file’s: the name out of both paragraphs and into this note, applied as a `life_replace`-only spec, `.tmp/sr-drafts/fix-06-21.json`, with the same change made in the day’s generator so that it still reproduces both folders, and the two rows then re-applied with `.tmp/sr-reapply-json.py`, which touches the json half only — `upgrade.py` could not have done it, its `row` branch asserting `undocumented` on a row by then `venerated`. Nothing was added to `scripts/related-floor-exclusions.json`, and **`theodosius-the-younger` takes no `related` row**: an emperor in a life is not automatically a relation, and one who signs a charter is a grantor and not a companion. WHAT ELSE IS NEW. The vow: „Одмалена васпитани у хришћанству, са заветом да ће живети увек у девству и служити цркви“ — brought up in Christianity from childhood with a vow to live always in virginity and to serve the church, which neither other book has, and **which does not give him a `virgin` type**, standing in the body where the heading gives Преподобни and only that. „Као два апостола“ — like two apostles — turning unbelievers into Christians through East and West, where saint.gr had the imitation of Paul; **a hundred churches built in their lifetime**, „Сазидаше стотину цркава за живота свога“, which is new and is a count and not a date. And the one line that is his alone: „Житељи Медиолана призивају светог Јулија у помоћ против вукова“ — the people of Mediolanum call on Saint Julius for help **against wolves**. No `office` — a presbyter’s order is not a see and no pack holds a phrase for it. No `locations`: Myrmidonia and Mediolanum are named in clauses, and the folder already carries Kousion and Lake Orta in prose. **No rows but the one added**: Theodosius the Younger is an emperor, and the wolves are not a folder. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse. **THE IDENTIFICATION IS MADE ON THE SCENE AND NOT ON THE NAME, AND IT IS THE DAY’S LONGEST READING.** This entry names two men with two of the commonest names in the corpus, which holds twenty-three `julian-*` folders and two `julius-*`. What identifies them is everything else. The Prologue: brothers, „Јулије беше презвитер а Јулијан ђакон“, brought up from childhood in Christianity with a vow of perpetual virginity and the service of the church, turning unbelievers in East and West like two apostles, building a hundred churches in their lifetime, and „Упокојили се мирно у Господу близу Медиолана“ — falling asleep in peace in the Lord **near Mediolanum**. `julius-of-aegina` and `julian-the-deacon-of-aegina` carry, off saint.gr, a presbyter and a deacon of exactly those two names who studied at Athens, came back to Aegina and **resolved together** to imitate Paul and preach Christ, were ordained by the bishop of Athens the one presbyter and the other deacon, went out **together** to preach and to baptise the gentiles, and ended the one at Kousion on **Lake Orta** and the other at Gozzano on **Lake Maggiore** — two lakes in the corner of Italy that Mediolanum stands in. Rank for rank, companionship for companionship, and the same end in the same country. The region agrees too, and it is the one word that had to be read rather than matched: this book has them „из грчке области Мирмидоније“, out of the Greek region of Myrmidonia, where saint.gr has them born on the Greek island of Aegina. **The two names are not matched as strings**, and nothing here turns on them: the identification stands on the presbyter-and-deacon pair, the joint mission and the death near Mediolanum, and would stand if the region were not named at all. `sr-namesweep.mjs` is useless on a company, scoring only the first name of one, and was not relied on; `ls saints | grep -iE 'julius|julian'` is what found them. THE VERSE IS NOT USED, AND ON THIS DAY THAT COSTS SOMETHING. The ПЕСМА for 21 June is the longest of the wave so far and it tells a scene the prose entry does not: Julian building a tomb for his brother Julius beside their ninety-ninth church, Julius telling him mildly to prepare himself, for the grave is built for him and he will go before his brother, and God appointing Julius to build the hundredth church on a lonely island. **It is Bishop Nikolai’s own verse and not the entry’s account**, and §3 of this wave’s brief puts the verse in no field and in no life; so the scene is recorded here, where a reading belongs, and written into neither paragraph. THE DAY’S THIRD ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER, AND THE CORPUS HAS ALREADY REFUSED THIS MAN ONCE. „Свети мученик Арчил II, цар грузињски“ — Archil II, king of Georgia, son of king Stephen and grandson of the great Georgian king Vakhtang, a great Christian and a protector of Christianity, tortured by the Muslims and beheaded for Christ on 20 March 744, being eighty years old when he suffered. `ls saints | grep -iE 'archil|luarsab'` returns nobody and `grep -ril Archil saints/*/saint.json` returns exactly one folder: `six-thousand-martyrs-of-david-gareji`, whose own attestation note already says that «the **king Archil of Georgia** gathered all the martyrs’ relics and buried them honourably» and that **«Arsenius and Archil are named as the entry names them and identified with nobody»**. So this is not a reader’s first refusal of Archil but the corpus’s second, and the two agree: he is named and he gets no folder. Ruling 3, therefore — and **20 March 744, the eighty years and the lineage are written nowhere**, the eighty years being a lifespan besides. `vakhtang-gorgasali` exists and takes no row and no mention in any prose written today: a grandfather is a kinship, but there is no grandson’s folder for it to be a kinship on. THE DAY’S FOURTH ENTRY IS REFUSED FOR WANT OF A FOLDER. „Свети мученик Луарсаб II, књаз карталински у Грузији“ — Luarsab II, prince of Kartli in Georgia, whose father George X also suffered for the faith and was poisoned by the Persian shah; thrown into a prison near Shiraz where he lay seven years, and then by the order of shah Abbas I hanged in the prison together with two servants, on 21 June 1622, with a heavenly light seen over his grave. `ls saints | grep -i luarsab` returns nobody, and `grep -ril Luarsab saints/*/saint.json` returns nobody either; `grep -ril Kartli` holds four Georgian folders and none of them is he. Ruling 3: named here, left out of every life written today, no folder from me, and **1622, the seven years, George X, Abbas I and the two servants are written nowhere**. The two servants are a narrated martyrdom with no name, which takes no row and no folder on the settled rule.
